 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Miami Heat continue their Western Conference road trip Monday when they visit the Los Angeles Lakers at Crypto.com Arena. The game brings together two franchises with championship expectations and features an interesting contrast between Miami's ability to generate offense and a Los Angeles team trying to establish consistency during the opening weeks of the NBA season.
 Miami enters the game following an impressive 145-125 victory over the Indiana Pacers on Friday. The Heat delivered one of their most productive offensive performances of the young season, demonstrating how dangerous they can become when their offense operates efficiently. The victory followed a 129-117 road win against Atlanta, giving Miami consecutive performances with at least 129 points.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Los Angeles is coming off a 131-125 victory over the Toronto Raptors on Sunday, bouncing back from a 112-95 defeat against Golden State on Friday. The Lakers have shown impressive offensive potential but have also experienced stretches when their defense struggles to contain opposing scorers.
 Monday's game offers an intriguing test for both teams. Miami will attempt to carry its recent scoring momentum into Los Angeles, while the Lakers look to build on Sunday's victory and protect their home floor.
 How to Watch Miami Heat at Los Angeles Lakers
 Day: Monday
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Start Time: 10 p.m. ET
 Location: Crypto.com Arena, Los Angeles, California
 TV Channels: S pectrum SportsNet in the Los Angeles market and WPLG Local 10 in the Miami market
 Live Stream: Spectrum SportsNet+ for eligible Lakers-market viewers, Local10+ in the Miami market and NBA League Pass for eligible out-of-market viewers
 There is no scheduled nationwide television broadcast. Viewing options depend on the viewer's location, with NBA League Pass available outside the teams' local markets, subject to blackout restrictions.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Miami's Offense Is Starting to Find Its Rhythm
 The Heat have demonstrated considerable offensive potential in their recent games. Miami scored 129 points against Atlanta before producing 145 against Indiana, showing that the team can create scoring opportunities in several different ways.
 Giannis Antetokounmpo gives Miami a powerful interior presence and an elite transition threat. His ability to attack the basket creates difficult defensive decisions for opponents, particularly when Miami's perimeter players are making shots.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bam Adebayo also remains important because of his defensive versatility, rebounding and ability to contribute offensively. The Heat will need that balance against a Lakers team capable of generating substantial offensive production.
 Lakers Look to Build on Sunday's Victory
 Los Angeles enters Monday following a six-point victory over Toronto.
 The Lakers scored 131 points against the Raptors, demonstrating their offensive capabilities after a disappointing performance against Golden State. Luka Doncic remains one of the NBA's most dangerous offensive players. His ability to create shots, control possessions and distribute the basketball makes him difficult to defend.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Austin Reaves also provides Los Angeles with another important scoring option. The Lakers will need to maintain their offensive efficiency while improving defensively against a Miami team that has scored at least 129 points in consecutive games.
 A Test of Offensive Execution
 Both teams have demonstrated the ability to score at a high level, creating the possibility of an entertaining game. Miami will attempt to attack the basket and generate opportunities in transition.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Los Angeles will look to use Doncic's playmaking and its perimeter shooting to control the offensive tempo. Rebounding and turnovers could become particularly important if the game develops into a high-scoring contest.
 The Lakers will also be playing on consecutive nights, potentially giving Miami an advantage in preparation and recovery.
 Monday's game tips off at 10 p.m. ET.
